scope: Targeted primary-source review, not a systematic review or global state-of-the-art ranking

papers.title: Semantic Structure and Correspondence in Prospective Trance-Channeled Communications Attributed to Extraterrestrial Intelligences
papers.readingDepth: Author institution abstract; selected publisher methods accessible in search index; public Figshare v1 code/results/protocol inspected; live publisher full text returned 403
papers.summary: Three experienced channelers answered standardized interviews across 28 topical areas. The authors report transformer-embedding correspondence of 0.65–0.79 across channelers for the same purported ETI and 0.75–0.88 within channeler across ETIs after residualization.
papers.application: Close comparator for structured same-question corpus design. Use matched questions and separate within-person from between-person comparisons.
papers.limitations: Three-person sample, not the YouTube population. Similarity does not establish truth or an ET source. Supplement lacks participant answer inputs and the supplied code export lacks explicit global-text chunking and within-channeler residualization; full results were not replicated.

papers.title: Qualitative Structure and Meaning in Prospective Trance-Channeled Communications Attributed to Extraterrestrial Intelligences
papers.readingDepth: Author institution abstract; publisher full text returned 403
papers.summary: The authors analyze prospectively collected interviews with reflexive thematic analysis, reporting recurring narrative frames and conceptual metaphors. They explicitly avoid ontological conclusions.
papers.application: Pair quantitative similarities with close reading, contextual notes, contrasting examples and stated alternative interpretations.
papers.limitations: Shares authors and the prospective research program with L01; do not count it as an independent replication. This review does not verify an unobserved entity or communication mechanism.

papers.title: Channelers’ Answers to Questions from Scientists: An Exploratory Study
papers.authors: Helané Wahbeh; Paolo Speirn; Luciano Pederzoli; Patrizio Tressoldi
papers.summary: Fifteen channelers answered ten scientific questions in channeled and non-channeled states. Three judges found low within-person cross-state correspondence and virtually no correspondence across channelers, while qualitative themes overlapped for some questions.
papers.application: Retain disconfirming findings and distinguish thematic overlap from response agreement. Compare equivalent question types and answer lengths.
papers.limitations: Different participants, prompts and measures from L01; the results cannot be pooled directly or treated as a clean contradiction.

papers.title: A qualitative exploratory analysis of channeled content
papers.authors: J. Anastasia; H. Wahbeh; A. Delorme; J. Okonsky
papers.summary: Thirteen adult trance channels answered a research-oriented prompt; analysis identified seven themes across scientific-methodology, channeling-process and open-ended-information categories.
papers.application: Demonstrates a small-corpus thematic analysis with an explicit eliciting question. Preserve prompt context when interpreting frequencies.
papers.limitations: Prompt-driven and not an ET-channel census. The author institution page lists August 1; journal issue is July–August, so only year is normalized.

papers.title: Sentence-BERT: Sentence Embeddings using Siamese BERT-Networks
papers.summary: Introduces sentence encoders whose representations can be compared with cosine similarity, avoiding joint inference for every sentence pair.
papers.application: Use a frozen documented encoder on matched text units; preserve model identifier, revision, language, truncation and normalization settings.
papers.limitations: Cosine similarity depends on model and corpus. It does not measure factual correctness or independent origins. This paper does not validate every later Sentence Transformers model.

papers.title: BERTopic: Neural topic modeling with a class-based TF-IDF procedure
papers.readingDepth: arXiv abstract and repository README sections
papers.summary: Combines document embeddings, clustering and class-based TF-IDF topic representations.
papers.application: Candidate for sufficiently rich transcript chunks; show representative source passages, outliers and robustness across parameters.
papers.limitations: Clustering sparse titles can produce unstable or entity-name-driven topics. BERTopic has not been executed merely because it is cited.

papers.title: MMTEB: Massive Multilingual Text Embedding Benchmark
papers.readingDepth: arXiv abstract, version history and ICLR acceptance metadata
papers.summary: Extends embedding evaluation across hundreds of tasks and languages, including long-document and instruction-related tasks.
papers.application: Choose candidate encoders by the task and languages actually present; reserve an in-domain evaluation set.
papers.limitations: Reported rankings belong to the paper’s evaluation snapshot and do not establish the best model for this domain or today.

papers.title: Qwen3 Embedding: Advancing Text Embedding and Reranking Through Foundation Models
papers.readingDepth: arXiv abstract, version history and official repository usage
papers.summary: Offers 0.6B, 4B and 8B embedding/reranking models and reports strong multilingual benchmark results.
papers.application: Candidate for a future multilingual comparison against a small baseline, with identical documents and local validation.
papers.limitations: No Qwen inference or benchmark was run by this literature workstream. Its state-of-the-art claim is historical and benchmark-specific.

papers.title: jina-embeddings-v5-text: Task-Targeted Embedding Distillation
papers.summary: Presents compact task-targeted models and reports competitive same-size performance, multilingual support and long-context inputs.
papers.application: Current alternative worth testing for clustering versus retrieval tasks after checking the selected model card and license.
papers.limitations: Abstract review only; no weights downloaded or scores reproduced. A 32k-token capacity does not eliminate length and genre confounding.

papers.title: Large Language Models Struggle to Describe the Haystack without Human Help: A Social Science-Inspired Evaluation of Topic Models
papers.summary: A user study on two datasets finds readable LLM topic labels can be too generic for domain-specific exploration; human supervision improves usefulness at an effort cost.
papers.application: Require specific labels, traceable examples, counterexamples and review of whether a label teaches anything about the corpus.
papers.limitations: This supports human validation, not a universal ranking of topic methods. A model-agent panel is not equivalent to the study’s human participants.

papers.title: LLM Reading Tea Leaves: Automatically Evaluating Topic Models with Large Language Models
papers.authors: Xiaohao Yang; He Zhao; Dinh Phung; Wray Buntine; Lan Du
papers.summary: Proposes WALM, a joint evaluation of document and topic semantic quality, and reports agreement with human judgments in its experiments.
papers.application: Optional complementary diagnostic beside traceable lexical baselines and manual review; record judge/model identity.
papers.limitations: An LLM judge can share biases with a generator; it must not replace direct source inspection or be labeled independent human review.

papers.title: Text as Data: The Promise and Pitfalls of Automatic Content Analysis Methods for Political Texts
papers.summary: Argues that automatic content analysis requires problem-specific validation and close reading.
papers.application: Treat units, sample construction and validity checks as part of the analysis; keep model outputs distinguishable from substantive claims.
papers.limitations: Political-text examples transfer as methodology, not as findings about channeling. Only the introduction was read in detail.

papers.title: Evaluating the Consistency of Word Embeddings from Small Data
papers.authors: Jelke Bloem; Antske Fokkens; Aurélie Herbelot
papers.summary: Studies embeddings from small philosophical corpora and shows consistency depends on data, model and term frequency.
papers.application: Use split-sample and leave-one-document-out stability checks; flag low-sample channels instead of overinterpreting their nearest neighbors.
papers.limitations: The original method concerns word embeddings, so applying its stability principle to sentence-level channel centroids is our adaptation.

papers.title: On the Robustness of Multilingual Text Embedding Rankings Across Learning Tasks, Languages, and Benchmark Datasets
papers.authors: Ana Gjorgjevikj; Barbara Koroušić Seljak; Tome Eftimov
papers.summary: Studies how multilingual model rankings change with dataset composition and aggregation choices.
papers.application: Report sensitivity to language mix and channel weighting rather than advertising one universal best embedding model.
papers.limitations: Preprint and abstract-level review; not independently replicated here.

papers.title: Reading Tea Leaves: How Humans Interpret Topic Models
papers.authors: Jonathan Chang; Sean Gerrish; Chong Wang; Jordan L. Boyd-Graber; David M. Blei
papers.summary: Shows held-out likelihood and human semantic interpretability can diverge.
papers.application: Add topic/document intrusion-style review and check examples, not only numeric model scores.
papers.limitations: Human review tasks are recommendations; this agent panel does not constitute a blinded human study.

papers.title: MTEB: Massive Text Embedding Benchmark
papers.authors: Niklas Muennighoff; Nouamane Tazi; Loïc Magne; Nils Reimers
papers.summary: Benchmarks embeddings over diverse tasks and finds no universal best method in its tested set.
papers.application: Use retrieval, clustering and semantic-similarity evaluations aligned with intended use.
papers.limitations: Older benchmark snapshot; not a current leaderboard claim.
